name: wedge-hybrid-cost
theory_gate_citation: docs/theory/README.md §3 and §4 close the wedge as a SHORTCUT, by the argument that the centre bit at time T lives on diagonal d = T and settle(T) ~ 1.34*T > T, so the TARGET cell is never settled. That argument does not cover the target's dependency cone, whose smaller-d cells settle well before the horizon. The fraction of the cone the wedge supplies has never been measured and is what decides whether further wedge work is worth doing.
notes: settle(d) is measured inside a finite horizon, so it is an UPPER bound on the true settling time. That direction is safe for a negative: it can only make the wedge look more useful than it is. The practical constant factor and the asymptotic exponent are reported separately.
